findings.title: Service link variable replaces the app's own setting
findings.cause: container worker exits after reading CACHE_PORT as a setting of its own, and Kubernetes set it: for every Service of the namespace the kubelet gives each container variables named after the Service (service links), and for Service cache that includes CACHE_PORT=tcp://10.96.159.131:6379, an address where the app expects a port number; its log says: "cannot reach the cache on port tcp://10.96.159.131:6379"; Deployment worker has 0 of 1 replicas ready

evidence.what: container worker exited with code 1 (Error), restarted 6 times
last lines of container worker's log (run that exited)
evidence.detail:
connecting to cache:tcp://10.96.159.131:6379
cannot reach the cache on port tcp://10.96.159.131:6379
wget: bad address 'cache:tcp:'

evidence.what: Service cache has cluster IP 10.96.159.131 and port 6379, so the kubelet sets CACHE_PORT=tcp://10.96.159.131:6379 in the namespace's containers
evidence.command: kubectl get service cache -n kd-service-link-env-collision -o jsonpath='{.spec.clusterIP}{" "}{.spec.ports[0].port}'

evidence.what: the pod does not set enableServiceLinks: false, and container worker defines no CACHE_PORT of its own
evidence.command: kubectl get pod worker-65cbbfb8c5-jh2pb -n kd-service-link-env-collision -o jsonpath='{.spec.enableServiceLinks}{" "}{.spec.containers[?(@.name=="worker")].env[*].name}'

findings.fix: Set enableServiceLinks: false in the pod spec, so the kubelet adds no such variables (the Service's DNS name still works), or define CACHE_PORT in the container's env, which wins over the service link, or rename the app's variable or the Service.
